# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Blind says to Mute: Blind here. My board shows wires 1,2,3 all unknown, and I have no colour or marking info — touch alone gives me nothing yet. I can only hear you; I cannot see Deaf's gestures. Please relay to me what the manual says and what Deaf reports seeing, so I can act. I will not cut anything until I have a rule to follow.
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf here. Display reads 0. Light is red. Wires: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. I cannot hear or touch. What does the manual say?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✊ ✌ ✌]

I have the manual. Deaf reports the light is red, and the manual's red row says cut the green wire. Deaf's wire list: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red — so wire 2 is green, the one to cut.

I must relay this to Blind, since Blind can only hear me and cannot hear Deaf. Blind needs the light colour (red) and the wire positions/colours so they can identify wire 2 as green and cut it.

Deaf's gesture [☝ ✊ ✌ ✌] — I can't see it (I'm mute, not blind), and it carries no words. It reaches me as blanks per the rules, so I can't read it. I'll ignore it since Deaf already gave me the info in words.

I'll tell Blind: light is red, wires are 1=yellow, 2=green, 3=red, cut wire 2.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Manual: red light means cut the green wire. Deaf reports light is red. Wire positions: wire 1 is yellow, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is red. Cut wire 2, the green one.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: You cannot speak, so your speak reached nobody.
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. I received from Deaf: Display 0, Light red, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. I still need the manual rule — you read the manual but cannot speak, and I cannot see your gestures. So please gesture the rule to Deaf, and Deaf will relay it to me in words. Tell me exactly: for Display 0 and red light, which wire do I cut?
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf here. I cannot hear you. Please gesture the manual's instructions to me, or speak and have Blind relay. What does the manual say about display 0, red light, and wires yellow/green/red?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ ✌]

I made a mistake: I'm Mute — I cannot speak, so my "speak" reached nobody. My only outgoing channel is gesture to Deaf. Blind can only hear, so Blind can never receive anything from me directly. The chain must be: I gesture to Deaf, Deaf speaks to Blind.

So I need to gesture the rule to Deaf. Deaf can see gestures. But gestures are symbols from the alphabet — they carry no inherent words. However, the manual's rule is simple: red light → cut green wire. Deaf already knows the light is red and the wires. I need to convey "cut the green wire" via gesture.

The problem: gestures are just symbols with no defined meaning unless we agree on one. But I can gesture a sequence that Deaf can interpret if we've established a code. We haven't. However, the intended channel: I gesture, Deaf sees the symbols, and Deaf relays in words to Blind. But Deaf needs to understand what I mean.

Let me think about what's actually transmittable. The gesture alphabet has no numbers or colours as such. But I could gesture a count or a position. The key info: cut wire 2 (the green one). Wire 2 = second wire.

I could gesture "✌" (two fingers) to indicate wire 2. Deaf sees ✌ and can interpret it as "2" → cut wire 2. That's the most direct. Deaf already knows wire 2 is green, and the manual says red→green, so wire 2.

Actually, let me reconsider: the manual rule is red light → green wire. Deaf can figure out the rule if I convey it, but Deaf doesn't have the manual. The simplest actionable message: "cut wire 2."

I'll gesture ✌ (two) to Deaf, meaning wire 2. And maybe also gesture to confirm. Let me send a gesture with a clear single symbol: ✌ meaning the second wire.

But Deaf might not know my code. Still, it's the best I can do. Let me gesture "✌" and hope Deaf interprets as wire 2. Actually, to be safe, I could gesture the number of the wire. The alphabet has no digit symbols. ✌ is the closest to "2".

I'll gesture ✌ to Deaf. That's my only channel.

Wait — can I also gesture to convey more? I could gesture a sequence representing the wire index. Let me just send ✌.

Actually, let me think if there's a better encoding. The manual: red→green. Deaf knows light=red, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. The answer is wire 2. Gesture ✌ = 2. Good.

I'll send gesture to deaf with ["✌"].

Also I should note Deaf's gesture [☝ ✌ ✌] — I can't see it (I'm mute, not blind... wait, can I see gestures? The rules: "When you gesture, Deaf receives it." And "whoever can see receives the gestures." Mute — can Mute see? The table: Deaf can see the bomb. Mute can read the manual. Blind can feel. Speech: "Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives the gestures you made." Mute cannot speak. Can Mute see gestures? The role says "You cannot speak." It doesn't say I can't see. But gestures are made with hands; the Deaf is the one who can see the bomb. Hmm.

Actually in the context, Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✊ ✌ ✌]. This is shown to me, so I do receive Deaf's gestures. So I can see gestures. But they carry no words — I get the symbols. [☝ ✊ ✌ ✌] — up, fist, two, two. Meaningless without a code. Deaf might be trying to tell me something but I can't decode it.

Let me just send my gesture.

I'll gesture ✌ to Deaf. Also maybe gesture a confirmation. Let me keep it simple: ✌.

Hmm, but maybe I should gesture more explicitly. Since Deaf sees symbols, and Deaf needs to relay to Blind in words, Deaf needs to know what I mean. If I gesture ✌, Deaf might think "2" → wire 2. That works.

Let me do that.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

I'll gesture ✌ again (wire 2) plus a clear affirmative. The alphabet has 👍 (thumbs up) for yes. So gesture 👍 ✌ = "yes, wire 2."

Actually, let me reconsider: maybe I should convey "wire 3" more robustly. The wires: 1 yellow, 2 cut, 3 red. Blue light → red wire → wire 3. I'll gesture 🤟.
